entities.name: Schistosomiasis
entities.description: A major neglected tropical parasitic disease caused by blood-dwelling digenetic trematodes of the genus Schistosoma, manifesting as acute Katayama syndrome, chronic urogenital schistosomiasis with terminal hematuria, or chronic intestinal and hepatosplenic disease with Symmers pipestem periportal fibrosis and non-cirrhotic portal hypertension.

entities.name: Freshwater Cercarial Percutaneous Penetration via Aquatic Snail Intermediate Hosts
entities.description: Percutaneous penetration of intact human skin by free-swimming, fork-tailed cercariae within seconds to minutes of contact with infested freshwater bodies (lakes, rivers, irrigation canals, dams) during domestic, occupational, or recreational water exposure, where specific freshwater snails (Biomphalaria, Bulinus, Oncomelania) act as obligatory intermediate hosts.

entities.name: Sub-Saharan Africa, Nile Basin, Neotropical and East Asian Endemic Regions
entities.description: Epidemiological exposure across geographic regions with established transmission, predominantly sub-Saharan Africa (>90% of global burden), the Nile River basin (Egypt, Sudan), the Middle East, parts of South America (Brazil, Venezuela, Suriname), the Caribbean, China (Yangtze river basin), the Philippines, and the Mekong River basin.

entities.name: Schistosoma haematobium
entities.description: Digenean blood trematode residing in the pelvic and vesical venous plexuses, shedding terminal-spined eggs into the urinary tract that trigger granulomatous inflammation, sandy patches, terminal hematuria, obstructive uropathy, and bladder squamous cell carcinoma.

entities.name: Schistosoma mansoni
entities.description: Digenean blood trematode residing in the inferior mesenteric venules, producing prominent lateral-spined eggs that lodge in the intestinal mucosa and embolize to intrahepatic portal venules, triggering intestinal polyposis and Symmers pipestem periportal fibrosis.

entities.name: Schistosoma japonicum
entities.description: Zoonotic blood fluke endemic to East and Southeast Asia (China, Philippines, Indonesia), dwelling in superior mesenteric venules with >40 mammalian reservoir hosts, shedding small eggs with a rudimentary lateral knob that cause severe hepatosplenic disease and cerebral neuroschistosomiasis.

entities.name: Schistosoma mekongi and Schistosoma intercalatum
entities.description: Localized schistosome species causing intestinal schistosomiasis; S. mekongi is endemic to the Mekong River basin in Cambodia and Laos, while S. intercalatum is localized to Central and West African rainforest regions.

entities.name: Painless Terminal Hematuria in Urogenital Disease
entities.description: The pathognomonic physical hallmark of active urogenital S. haematobium schistosomiasis, occurring in >80% of affected children and adolescents, characterized by bright red blood voided selectively at the final conclusion of micturition due to detrusor contraction against egg-infiltrated bladder mucosa.

entities.name: Preserved Hepatic Synthetic Function Despite Severe Presinusoidal Portal Hypertension
entities.description: Critical diagnostic hallmark of chronic hepatosplenic schistosomiasis: intact hepatocellular protein synthesis and coagulation (normal serum albumin, normal PT/INR, absence of jaundice, absence of spider angiomas, and absence of hepatic encephalopathy) in the presence of massive splenomegaly, caput medusae, and catastrophic esophageal variceal hemorrhage.

entities.name: Acute Katayama Syndrome with Serum Sickness-Like Hypersensitivity Reaction
entities.description: Systemic immune-complex hypersensitivity syndrome occurring 2 to 8 weeks after initial cercarial exposure in non-immune individuals, characterized by abrupt high-spiking fevers, shaking chills, generalized urticaria, periorbital angioedema, nocturnal dry cough, wheezing, prostration, and tender hepatosplenomegaly.

entities.name: Cystoscopic Sandy Patches and Bladder Granulomatous Pseudopolyps
entities.description: Pathognomonic cystoscopic appearance in urogenital schistosomiasis showing submucosal calcified degenerated egg clusters resembling grains of beach sand (sandy patches) alongside hyperplastic inflammatory pseudopolyps in the bladder mucosa.

entities.name: Acute Lumbosacral Myeloradiculopathy via Batson Vertebral Venous Plexus
entities.description: Severe ectopic neuroschistosomiasis manifestation (predominantly S. mansoni) where eggs travel through Batson valveless vertebral venous plexus into the spinal cord, presenting as acute transverse myelitis or subacute myeloradiculopathy with flaccid paraplegia, T11-L1 sensory level, and urinary retention.

entities.name: Female Genital Schistosomiasis with Sandy Patches and Post-Coital Bleeding
entities.description: Urogenital involvement in women presenting with granulomatous vulvovaginal and cervical sandy patches, contact/post-coital bleeding, pelvic dyspareunia, subfertility, and markedly heightened biological susceptibility to HIV acquisition.

entities.name: Symmers Clay-Pipe Stem Periportal Fibrosis on Ultrasound
entities.description: Bedside abdominal ultrasound findings (WHO Niamey protocol) demonstrating dense, echogenic fibrous sleeves collar-wrapping intrahepatic portal vein branches (pipestem, doughnut, or bullseye sign, cuff thickness >4-6 mm) with dilated main portal vein (>12-14 mm), massive splenomegaly, and preserved smooth liver margins.

entities.name: Urine Polycarbonate Membrane Filtration Revealing Terminal-Spined Eggs
entities.description: Gold standard admission microscopic parasitology for S. haematobium: polycarbonate or nylon filter filtration of 10 mL daytime urine (collected between 10:00 and 14:00) identifying characteristic large, oval, transparent eggs (110-170 x 40-70 µm) bearing a sharp, distinct terminal spine.

entities.name: Kato-Katz Smear Revealing Lateral-Spined or Lateral-Knobbed Schistosome Eggs
entities.description: Microscopic examination of fecal smears via Kato-Katz thick smear or formalin-ether concentration demonstrating golden-brown eggs with a prominent, sharp lateral spine (S. mansoni, 114-180 x 45-70 µm) or smaller subglobular eggs with an inconspicuous lateral knob (S. japonicum, 70-100 x 50-70 µm).

entities.name: Striking Peripheral Blood Eosinophilia on Admission CBC
entities.description: Complete blood count hallmark demonstrating dramatic peripheral eosinophilia (>20-50% of differential, absolute eosinophil count >3,000-8,000/µL) during acute Katayama syndrome, and persistent mild-to-moderate eosinophilia (5-15%) in chronic active infections.

entities.name: Point-of-Care Urine Circulating Cathodic Antigen Detection
entities.description: Rapid lateral flow urine cassette test (POC-CCA) detecting regurgitated gut proteoglycans of active, living adult Schistosoma mansoni flukes within 20 minutes with high sensitivity at admission/triage.

entities.name: Urinary Tract Ultrasound Demonstrating Bladder Wall Thickening and Hydroureteronephrosis
entities.description: Bedside urinary tract sonography showing irregular, thickened bladder mucosa (>5 mm), luminal pseudopolyps, bladder wall calcifications, and obstructive ureterovesical pathology leading to unilateral or bilateral hydroureter and hydronephrosis.

entities.name: Complete Absence of Freshwater Immersion or Exposure in Endemic Regions
entities.description: Total lack of any lifetime or travel-related exposure to freshwater bodies (lakes, rivers, ponds, irrigation streams) in recognized schistosomiasis-endemic regions effectively rules out schistosome infection.

entities.name: Total Absence of Microscopic Hematuria on Urinalysis Dipsticks and Normal Bladder Ultrasound
entities.description: Complete absence of microhematuria on repeated reagent strip urinalyses combined with entirely normal bladder wall thickness and architecture on ultrasound virtually excludes active urogenital S. haematobium infection.

entities.name: Absence of Peripheral Blood Eosinophilia During Acute Febrile Presentation
entities.description: Absence of peripheral eosinophilia on admission complete blood count during an acute febrile multisystem illness following freshwater contact strongly argues against acute Katayama syndrome schistosomiasis.

entities.name: Cirrhosis of the Liver
entities.description: Diffuse chronic end-stage parenchymal liver disease characterized by architectural distortion, regenerative nodules, and severe hepatocellular synthetic impairment (hypoalbuminemia, prolonged PT/INR, direct hyperbilirubinemia, and hepatic encephalopathy).

entities.name: Visceral Leishmaniasis
entities.description: Systemic protozoan infection caused by Leishmania donovani species complex, characterized by prolonged undulating fevers, massive splenomegaly, pancytopenia without eosinophilia, and intracellular Leishman-Donovan bodies in bone marrow or splenic tissue.

entities.name: Bacterial Urinary Tract Infection
entities.description: Acute bacterial cystitis or pyelonephritis caused by uropathogens (e.g., E. coli), presenting with dysuria throughout micturition, pyuria, positive urine nitrite/leukocyte esterase, positive bacterial culture, and response to standard antibacterial therapy.

entities.name: Urothelial Bladder Carcinoma
entities.description: Primary transitional cell carcinoma of the urinary bladder typically arising in older individuals with a history of tobacco exposure, manifesting as painless continuous hematuria and irregular exophytic papillary masses on cystoscopy.

entities.name: Praziquantel Chemotherapy
entities.description: Oral anthelmintic agent of choice (40 mg/kg for S. haematobium/S. mansoni; 60 mg/kg for S. japonicum/S. mekongi) causing rapid tegumental vacuolization, calcium influx, muscular paralysis, and immune-mediated clearance of adult schistosomes, achieving >90% egg excretion reduction and >75-90% cure rates.

entities.name: Systemic Corticosteroid Suppression for Acute Katayama Syndrome
entities.description: Corticosteroid therapy (prednisone 0.5-2.0 mg/kg/day) that suppresses severe immune-complex hypersensitivity, pulmonary infiltrates, and systemic inflammation in acute Katayama syndrome before introducing delayed praziquantel once worms reach maturity.

entities.name: Praziquantel Refractoriness in Immature Migrating Schistosomula
entities.description: Biological insensitivity of juvenile migrating schistosomula (<4-6 weeks of age) to praziquantel; premature praziquantel monotherapy fails to kill immature larvae and may precipitate severe paradoxical immune reactions in acute infection.

entities.name: Standard Antibacterial and Antiprotozoal Agents
entities.description: Standard antimicrobial classes (fluoroquinolones, cephalosporins, cotrimoxazole, metronidazole) which lack any antiparasitic activity against Schistosoma trematodes and result in complete therapeutic non-response.

relationships.target: Freshwater Cercarial Percutaneous Penetration via Aquatic Snail Intermediate Hosts
relationships.description: [TRANSMITTED_BY] Transmission occurs via direct percutaneous penetration of intact human skin by free-swimming cercariae shed by intermediate aquatic snail hosts (Biomphalaria, Bulinus, Oncomelania) during contact with infested freshwater lakes, rivers, or canals.

relationships.target: Sub-Saharan Africa, Nile Basin, Neotropical and East Asian Endemic Regions
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Epidemiological exposure in high-risk geographic areas, predominantly sub-Saharan Africa (>90% of global cases), Egypt/Sudan (Nile basin), parts of South America, the Caribbean, China, the Philippines, and Southeast Asia.

relationships.target: Schistosoma haematobium
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Caused by Schistosoma haematobium, an adult blood fluke residing in the vesical and pelvic venous plexuses that sheds terminal-spined eggs, driving urogenital inflammation, hematuria, and bladder malignancy.

relationships.target: Schistosoma mansoni
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Caused by Schistosoma mansoni, inhabiting the inferior mesenteric venules and shedding lateral-spined eggs into the liver and colonic wall to trigger intestinal ulceration and Symmers periportal fibrosis.

relationships.target: Schistosoma japonicum
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Caused by Schistosoma japonicum, a zoonotic blood fluke inhabiting the superior mesenteric venules with mammalian reservoir hosts, inducing aggressive hepatosplenic fibrosis and cerebral neuroschistosomiasis.

relationships.target: Schistosoma mekongi and Schistosoma intercalatum
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Caused by regional schistosome species Schistosoma mekongi (endemic to the Mekong River basin) and Schistosoma intercalatum (endemic to central and western Africa), producing localized intestinal schistosomiasis.

relationships.target: Painless Terminal Hematuria in Urogenital Disease
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Painless, bright red hematuria occurring selectively at the very end of micturition is present in >80% of children and adolescents with urogenital S. haematobium, resulting from terminal contraction of the egg-studded bladder wall.

relationships.target: Preserved Hepatic Synthetic Function Despite Severe Presinusoidal Portal Hypertension
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Critical hallmark of advanced hepatosplenic schistosomiasis: intact hepatic synthetic capacity (normal serum albumin, normal INR/PT, absence of jaundice, and absence of hepatic encephalopathy) despite massive splenomegaly, caput medusae, and life-threatening bleeding esophageal varices due to pure presinusoidal portal block sparing lobular parenchyma.

relationships.target: Acute Katayama Syndrome with Serum Sickness-Like Hypersensitivity Reaction
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] High-spiking abrupt fevers, rigors, generalized urticaria, facial angioedema, nocturnal dry cough, wheezing, and tender hepatosplenomegaly arising 2 to 8 weeks post-immersion in non-immune individuals, provoked by circulating immune complexes against maturing schistosomula and initial oviposition.

relationships.target: Cystoscopic Sandy Patches and Bladder Granulomatous Pseudopolyps
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Direct visual inspection or cystoscopy reveals classic sandy patches (rough, yellowish calcified ovular submucosal aggregations resembling beach sand) and hyperplastic granulomatous pseudopolyps in the bladder mucosa.

relationships.target: Acute Lumbosacral Myeloradiculopathy via Batson Vertebral Venous Plexus
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Ectopic migration of schistosome eggs (predominantly S. mansoni) via Batson valveless vertebral venous plexus leads to acute spinal granulomatous compression, presenting with acute or subacute flaccid paraplegia, a sharp sensory level at T11-L1, lumbar radicular pain, and neurogenic urinary retention.

relationships.target: Female Genital Schistosomiasis with Sandy Patches and Post-Coital Bleeding
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Granulomatous cervical, vaginal, and vulvar lesions featuring mucosal sandy patches, contact bleeding, post-coital hemorrhage, dyspareunia, and an elevated vulnerability to HIV acquisition.

relationships.target: Symmers Clay-Pipe Stem Periportal Fibrosis on Ultrasound
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Point-of-care abdominal ultrasound (WHO Niamey protocol) demonstrates distinctive echogenic fibrous cuffs surrounding intrahepatic portal branches (pipestem, doughnut, or bullseye sign, periportal wall thickness >4-6 mm) with main portal vein dilation (>12-14 mm) and smooth liver surface contour.

relationships.target: Urine Polycarbonate Membrane Filtration Revealing Terminal-Spined Eggs
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Microscopic filtration of 10 mL midday urine (collected between 10:00 and 14:00) through polycarbonate or nylon filters reveals definitive large transparent eggs (110-170 x 40-70 µm) bearing a sharp, terminal apical spine pathognomonic of Schistosoma haematobium.

relationships.target: Kato-Katz Smear Revealing Lateral-Spined or Lateral-Knobbed Schistosome Eggs
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Stool Kato-Katz thick smear or formalin-ether concentration microscopically demonstrates diagnostic golden-brown eggs with a prominent sharp lateral spine (S. mansoni, 114-180 x 45-70 µm) or subglobular eggs with a subtle lateral knob (S. japonicum, 70-100 x 50-70 µm).

relationships.target: Striking Peripheral Blood Eosinophilia on Admission CBC
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Peripheral blood complete blood count on admission exhibits prominent eosinophilia (>20-50% of white blood cell differential, absolute count >3,000-8,000/µL in acute Katayama syndrome; 5-15% persistent eosinophilia in chronic phases).

relationships.target: Point-of-Care Urine Circulating Cathodic Antigen Detection
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Urine POC-CCA lateral flow dipstick test detects regurgitated adult worm gut proteoglycans within 20 minutes, serving as a rapid, sensitive biomarker for active Schistosoma mansoni infection.

relationships.target: Urinary Tract Ultrasound Demonstrating Bladder Wall Thickening and Hydroureteronephrosis
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Bedside ultrasound of the urinary tract displays irregular thickening of the bladder wall (>5 mm), pseudopolyps, calcified bladder wall margins, ureteric strictures, and unilateral or bilateral hydroureter and hydronephrosis.

relationships.target: Complete Absence of Freshwater Immersion or Exposure in Endemic Regions
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Absolute lack of history of recreational, domestic, or occupational skin contact with freshwater bodies in an endemic transmission zone effectively excludes schistosomiasis as the underlying etiology.

relationships.target: Total Absence of Microscopic Hematuria on Urinalysis Dipsticks and Normal Bladder Ultrasound
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Persistent, complete absence of microhematuria across multiple chemical reagent dipsticks coupled with completely normal bladder wall morphology on ultrasound virtually excludes active urogenital Schistosoma haematobium disease.

relationships.target: Absence of Peripheral Blood Eosinophilia During Acute Febrile Presentation
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Complete absence of peripheral blood eosinophilia during an acute febrile multisystem illness following freshwater immersion strongly argues against acute Katayama syndrome.

relationships.target: Cirrhosis of the Liver
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from cirrhosis of the liver because hepatosplenic schistosomiasis causes pure presinusoidal portal hypertension that preserves normal hepatic synthetic function (normal albumin, normal coagulation PT/INR, absence of jaundice or encephalopathy) and maintains a smooth liver contour with ultrasound periportal pipestem collars, whereas cirrhosis displays diffuse parenchymal nodularity, small shrunken liver, and marked hepatocellular functional failure.

relationships.target: Visceral Leishmaniasis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from visceral leishmaniasis (kala-azar) which causes chronic undulating fever, profound pancytopenia without eosinophilia, and intracellular Leishman-Donovan amastigotes on bone marrow aspirate, whereas chronic hepatosplenic schistosomiasis is predominantly afebrile, preserves leukocyte lines, features peripheral eosinophilia, and exhibits Symmers periportal fibrosis.

relationships.target: Bacterial Urinary Tract Infection
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from bacterial urinary tract infection which typically produces initial or continuous dysuria, significant pyuria, positive nitrite/leukocyte esterase, positive bacterial urine cultures, and swift clearance with antibacterial therapy, whereas urogenital schistosomiasis is characterized by terminal hematuria, eosinophilia, terminal-spined eggs, and total refractoriness to antibacterial agents.

relationships.target: Urothelial Bladder Carcinoma
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Differentiated from transitional cell urothelial carcinoma which presents in older patients with heavy tobacco exposure with continuous hematuria and exophytic transitional cell bladder masses, whereas schistosomal bladder pathology occurs in younger exposed patients, produces squamous cell carcinoma rather than urothelial carcinoma, shows bladder mural calcification, and demonstrates terminal-spined eggs on microscopy.

relationships.target: Praziquantel Chemotherapy
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Patent mature schistosome infections demonstrate high parasitological cure and >90-95% egg reduction following oral praziquantel (40 mg/kg for S. mansoni/S. haematobium; 60 mg/kg for S. japonicum/S. mekongi), which disrupts parasite tegumental calcium channels and provokes immune-mediated clearance.

relationships.target: Systemic Corticosteroid Suppression for Acute Katayama Syndrome
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Acute Katayama syndrome responds promptly to systemic corticosteroids (prednisone 0.5-2.0 mg/kg/day) by blunting life-threatening immune-complex hypersensitivity and tissue edema, allowing safe bridging to delayed praziquantel once worms mature.

relationships.target: Praziquantel Refractoriness in Immature Migrating Schistosomula
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Immature migrating schistosomula (<4-6 weeks old) are intrinsically refractory to praziquantel, causing treatment failure if praziquantel is administered alone prematurely during early pre-patent infection.

relationships.target: Standard Antibacterial and Antiprotozoal Agents
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Schistosoma flukes are intrinsically unresponsive to standard antibacterial (e.g., fluoroquinolones, penicillins), antifungal, and antiprotozoal drugs, failing to clear infection or abate egg excretion despite symptom overlap with bacterial cystitis or dysentery.
